sector_model: enterprise software platform: GAAP P/E, EV/sales, FCF before and after SBC, net debt after acquisition financing, RPO, goodwill share of assets
thesis: ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW; 5-for-1 split Dec 2025) sells subscription workflow software. Q3 2026 revenue 4,106M (+20.5%; includes Armis and Veza acquisitions), subscription 3,988M (+20.9%); 9M revenue 11,863M (+22.2%); non-cancellable RPO 29.7B. GAAP operating income Q3 385M (9.4% margin vs 16.8%) and 9M 1,050M vs 1,381M; 9M OCF 3,096M vs 3,206M, capex 346M. TTM revenue 15,431M, GAAP NI 1,445M, OCF 5,334M, capex 584M, FCF 4,750M, SBC 2,323M. Debt 7,524M (commercial paper 2,100M principal, senior notes 5,500M) vs cash and marketable securities 6,961M: net debt about 563M versus about 8.6B net cash at 2025 year-end after 9.2B of 2026 acquisitions (Armis 7.6B, Veza 1.2B). At 100.66 (2026-11-12 close; 52-week 81.24-175.00): market cap about 104.5B on 1,037.9M shares, EV about 105.0B, 6.8x TTM sales, 72x TTM GAAP earnings, FCF yield 4.5% (2.3% after SBC). Growth is strong but the price is down about 42% from the 52-week high, so the market is already doubting something; cheapness is not shown at 72x GAAP earnings.
counterthesis: GAAP margins fell sharply after the acquisitions (Q3 operating margin 9.4% vs 16.8%), SBC is about 15% of revenue, so FCF after SBC yield is only 2.3%. Reported 2026 growth is inflated by 7.6B Armis and 1.2B Veza; organic growth is unread. 9M net income includes 367M of upward strategic-investment gains. Goodwill rose from 3.6B to 10.0B and intangibles from 1.1B to 3.6B, so impairment risk and amortization drag now matter. One US federal channel partner is 12% of revenue and 20% of receivables. A workforce restructuring started in 2026 (amount unread). Concern about AI agents displacing seat-based software may explain the de-rating and has not been tested. Peers, guidance, cRPO, risk factors and the 10-K unread.
invalidation: Thesis weakens if organic subscription growth falls below high teens, GAAP operating margin stays below 12% after integration, federal concentration cuts hit revenue, or buybacks keep being funded by commercial paper. A valuation case needs FCF yield after SBC well above 4% or evidence of stable margin recovery.
